inputs.share_count_basis: 2,378,185,860 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim note 17) less 39,288,400 shares bought back and cancelled 2-14 July 2026 (34,000,400 + 5,000,000 + 288,000; interim note 22) = 2,338,897,460. No options or share awards outstanding; the HK$1,960m zero-coupon CB due June 2027 (83.26m conversion shares at HK$23.54) is out of the money at the current price and is carried as debt in the bridge rather than as dilution -- conversion would add 3.6% to the count and remove RMB1,671m of debt, roughly value-neutral at the conversion price. Count held FLAT because SBC (zero) is expensed in the flows.
inputs.cash_composition: Cash and bank balances 3,295.4 + restricted cash 6,525.5 (short-term offshore deposits pledged as collateral for the bank borrowings -- the rate-arbitrage structure) + non-pledged long-term bank deposits 360.5 + wealth-management products at FVTPL 953.5 = 11,134.9. All RMB millions at 30 June 2026 (interim note 14 and balance sheet). total_debt is the short-term interest-bearing bank borrowings only (all current at 30 June 2026); lease liabilities (92.0) excluded under lease treatment B.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income was RMB186.6m (FY2025 AR line 1149), mostly earned on the pledged deposits. It is NOT inside reported FCF: the cash-flow statement deducts it from PBT in the OCF reconciliation and books 'Interest received' (153.5m) in investing activities, so OCF - capex already excludes it. Deducting it again would double-strip. The matching assets (restricted cash, deposits, WMP) are in the bridge at face, and the arbitrage spread (interest income less the 74.1m finance cost on the borrowings) is deliberately given no value.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR cash-flow reconciliation and H1 FY2026 interim: no share-based payment expense in FY2024, FY2025 or H1 FY2026 (FY2023: RMB55.5m pre-IPO, line 739 FY2024 AR). A post-IPO share scheme exists but has made no grants. SBC-zero: house and street bases coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY2025 or in the six months to 30 June 2026. HK$798.8m (~RMB681m) of buybacks on 2-14 July 2026 are post-balance-date and are charged in equity_bridge, with the share count reduced to match -- never both counted in the count and omitted from cash.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1729 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-16T10:31Z. All per-share values are computed in CNY and multiplied by 1.1729 to HKD; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD so they compare to current_price. No dual listing exists for a parity check; cross-check: the HK$1,960m CB principal converts to RMB1,671m at this rate, consistent with the RMB1,673m net-proceeds figure used in the bridge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' currency: 10y China Government Bond ~1.8%, China equity risk premium ~7.5% (mature-market 4.5% plus country/governance premium for a Cayman-incorporated PRC consumer franchisor), beta ~1.0 for a mass-market consumer franchise -> cost of equity ~9.3%; the gross bank debt is collateralised by restricted deposits and is economically a wash, so WACC ~= CoE. 9.5% used, identical across scenarios -- risk is charged in the flows (bear weight 25%, bear margins), not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: B (leases as operating cost): the full lease payment (FY2025 principal 58.1 + interest 2.3 = RMB60.5m, 0.47% of revenue) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path 0.5%, and lease liabilities (RMB92.0m at 30 June 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (~0.9% of revenue vs 1.3% total) so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI is immaterial (RMB13.6m book at 30 June 2026, loss-making in H1 FY2026) and is deducted once in equity_bridge at book.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US'), with the adaptations file applied (dual currency, leases B, NCI, matching-asset rule, SBC-zero). Guming is a franchisor/supply-chain operator -- 96.5% of FY2025 revenue is goods, equipment and management services sold to ~7,100 franchisees -- so its value is a stream of free cash flow and the standard engine applies; it is not a REIT, bank or holdco. FY0 is FY2025 (31 Dec year-end); Y1 = FY2026. FCF BASE: reported FCF FY2025 = OCF 2,408.6 - capex 248.3 = 2,160.3. The RMB556.9m fair-value gain on the pre-IPO preferred shares is non-cash and already excluded from OCF (it is reversed in the OCF reconciliation), so no normalisation of the FCF base is needed; it does, however, inflate the EBITDA/NetIncome columns in the Metrics CSV, so the FY2025 margin anchor used here is the EBITDA EX the gain and ex interest income: (PBT 3,758.6 + finance costs 74.1 - interest income 186.6 - FV gain 556.9 + D&A 164.7) / 12,913.8 = 25.2%; company adjusted EBITDA 3,365.7 = 26.1%; H1 FY2026 on the same basis 26.0% (26.4% ex the 84.7m FX loss). GEARING: the 64.9% reported gearing is a cash-and-yield-management structure -- RMB6.5bn of offshore short-term deposits pledged against RMB5.6bn of short-term bank loans -- not operating leverage; both legs are in the bridge at face and net to a cash surplus. WORKING CAPITAL: distributor profile (inventory + franchisee receivables > payables); FY2025 WC consumed ~RMB350m on a 4,122m revenue increase (~ -8%), H1 FY2026 released cash seasonally; wc_capture -5% base. TAX: FY2025 effective rate 20.1% on PBT ex the non-taxable gain, lifted by withholding tax on PRC-subsidiary distributions as dividends grow; path ramps 21% -> 23%. CAPEX: 1.9% FY2025, 5.1% FY2024, 5.2% FY2023; 2.5% used near term (warehouse/cold-chain build-out, CB proceeds earmarked partly for equipment) tapering to 2.2%. DIVIDEND: contrary to the Analysis JSON, the Board declared NO interim dividend for H1 FY2026 (interim p.49); the RMB1,034m declared in H1 FY2026 was the FY2025 final (HK$0.50/sh) and RMB1,085m of it was still payable at 30 June 2026, so it is deducted in the bridge. PRICE: regular-session close, not volatile.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: 3-year forward revenue CAGR of the base-case path (FY2025->FY2028: 25%/15%/10%). Historical CAGRs of 31-48% are a store-rollout phase that the category's deceleration (industry growth ~25% in 2021 to ~7% in 2026) and management's shift to stricter site selection make unrepeatable.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not computable: shareholders' equity was negative in FY2021-FY2022 (RMB-1,206m, -817m) because the pre-IPO preferred shares were carried as liabilities at fair value, then jumped on the Feb-2025 IPO reclassification. Revenue (3yr 32.4%), adjusted profit (3yr 48.4%) and owner FCF (2yr 38.9%) are the usable series; FCF history is only FY2023-FY2025 (no cash-flow statement in the FY2021-22 rows). Owner-FCF CAGR exceeds reported-FCF CAGR only because FY2023 carried RMB55.5m of pre-IPO SBC; SBC has been zero since.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY2022 5,559.2 -> FY2025 12,913.8; FY2021 4,383.9 -> FY2025. Diluted EPS FY2023 0.58 -> FY2025 1.08 (FY2025 includes the RMB556.9m FV gain; ex-gain ~0.89, CAGR ~24%). Company adjusted profit FY2022 788.1 -> FY2025 2,574.8. Reported FCF FY2023 1,174.5 -> FY2025 2,160.3; owner FCF FY2023 1,119.0 (after 55.5 SBC) -> 2,160.3.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +25%: H1 was +31.9% on stores +28.4% YoY and GMV +40%, but H2 laps the FY2025 delivery-subsidy peak, net store adds slowed (1,318 opened in H1 FY2026 vs 1,570) and management has moved to stricter site selection. FY2027 +15% and FY2028 +10% as store growth settles to ~10%/8% with coffee and sixth-generation store upgrades adding low-single-digit per-store growth; fading to 2.5% as the category matures at ~7% industry growth and Guming's share gains slow.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 EBITDA ex the FV gain and ex interest income 25.2% (company adjusted EBITDA 26.1%); H1 FY2026 26.0-26.4% with H2 seasonally stronger. 26.5% in FY2026 rising to 27.5% as warehouse density and procurement scale lift gross margin (30.6% -> 33.0% -> 33.4% over FY2024-H1 FY2026) while franchisee-support and logistics spend cap the operating leverage.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 15x FCF (not 20x): a mass-market tea franchisor in a saturating, low-differentiation category with Mixue three times its size does not merit a compounder exit multiple.

scenario_narratives.base: Guming keeps compounding as the clear #2 mass-market tea franchisor: FY2026 revenue +25% (H1 +31.9% fading in H2 as delivery subsidies lap), store growth settling to ~10% in FY2027 and ~8% in FY2028 as densification of the existing 17 provinces and selective entry into adjacent ones continues, with coffee (12,000+ machine-equipped stores) and sixth-generation store upgrades adding low-single-digit per-store growth. Supply-chain scale lifts EBITDA margin (ex interest income and the FY2025 FV gain) from ~25-26% to 27.5%, while logistics subsidies to franchisees and ongoing warehouse capex (2.2-2.5% of revenue) cap operating leverage. Growth decays to 2.5% by FY2035 as the category's growth converges on ~7% and share gains slow. Cash tax ramps 21% -> 23% as withholding tax on distributed profits grows with dividends.
scenario_narratives.bull: Store rollout runs longer and faster than the category: Guming enters most of the 17 untouched provinces, closures stay low because per-store franchisee profit keeps rising after the 2025 delivery-price increase, and coffee plus dessert/snack lines lift purchase frequency so revenue grows 28%/20%/15% over FY2026-28. Procurement scale and a maturing warehouse network push EBITDA margin to 29.5%; capex runs higher (3%) early to build the capacity. Overseas entry (CB proceeds earmarked) is an option not modelled. Sell-side targets around HK$36 broadly sit in this case.
scenario_narratives.bear: The category saturates and churn bites: industry closures already run close to openings, Mixue's price leadership and premium players squeeze Guming's mid-price position, delivery-subsidy withdrawal exposes weak same-store trends, and franchisee returns compress so new openings dry up by FY2028 and the network shrinks modestly in FY2029 (revenue -2%). Guming absorbs more of the logistics and marketing burden to keep franchisees whole, taking EBITDA margin to 21%; receivables stretch (wc_capture -8%) and preferential tax rates roll off (25%). The balance sheet is not a solvency axis -- the bank debt is collateralised by deposits and nets to a cash surplus -- so the bear case is an earnings-power, not a going-concern, outcome.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: a single-country, single-brand franchisor in a category whose growth has fallen from ~25% to ~7% in five years, with elevated franchisee churn (652 closures FY2025, 521 in H1 FY2026) and a price-leading competitor three times its size; no going-concern axis, so not higher. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs store growth, margin expansion and franchisee economics all to hold at once against that backdrop. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Guming on the owner cash flow of its franchise supply chain, not on headline earnings: strip the FY2025 RMB557m non-cash preferred-share gain from the margin anchor, give no value to the interest-rate arbitrage (restricted deposits and the matching bank loans both at face, interest income outside the flows), charge leases once inside EBIT, hold the share count at the post-buyback figure and treat the out-of-the-money convertible as debt. The franchise model converts ~17% of revenue into owner FCF with almost no SBC, so the valuation turns on how long store growth lasts and whether the EBITDA margin holds in the 26-28% range as the category matures -- hence a 15x terminal cap and a heavier-than-default bear weight rather than a higher discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Store-network saturation and franchisee churn: revenue is goods sold to franchisees, so a stall in net openings or a rise in closures hits the top line directly (bear case).
Mixue price leadership and delivery-platform subsidy dynamics compressing per-store GMV and forcing Guming to absorb franchisee margin.
Chinese consumer spending slowdown; 100% mainland exposure with no diversification.
Food-safety or brand incident across a decentralised network of ~7,100 franchisees.

Treasury structure: RMB5.6bn of short-term bank loans against RMB6.5bn of pledged offshore deposits plus a HK$1.96bn CB due June 2027 -- rollover/counterparty complexity, though it nets to a cash surplus.
FX: CNY flows against an HKD quote; a 5% CNY move shifts the HKD value one-for-one.
Withholding tax on distributed PRC profits rising faster than the modelled 21% -> 23% path as payouts grow.
